contract_promises_exercised_20261001.schedule_authority_corrected: the merged handoff attachment names docs/current/DSH-BACKEND-CONTRACT-20260927.md as a current authority, and reading it exposed a real defect in the contract written on this branch. Its section 9.2 says /learning/reviews reports schedule_authority unavailable without an fsrs interpreter; this branch said placeholder_ladder. contract_promises_exercised_20261001.search_semantics_and_body_fields: the gap map section 2C recorded search filter/paging/sort semantics and index behaviour after a knowledge revision as unverified. Measured: GET /api/v1/search takes only q and active_only - there is no limit, offset, sort or page, and the limit is a hardcoded 20 - so two of the four do not exist to verify. active_only=true excludes a superseded revision and keeps its successor while the unfiltered call lists it with active false. The index cannot go stale across a revision because search::reindex deletes and rebuilds knowledge_fts from the knowledge table before every query; measured after a human correction the corrected wording is found under the successor, the superseded wording under the old revision, and an untouched sibling is unaffected. Reaching that cost a third instance of one mistake: the corrected text goes in new_body and sending body is silently ignored, so the successor was a clone of the old revision. The contract now lists the exact field names for all thirteen routes plus the nested v3 body, and tests/maintenance/test_request_body_fields.py asserts that list against the structs. It also corrected two field facts: status and created_by are required on knowledge creation, and correct is required on a learning event.
contract_promises_exercised_20261001.review_cost: docs/architecture/CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE.md records that the review route waits for the FSRS worker inside the single-writer callback; the branch contract did not carry that and it was never measured here. Measured, five reviews each way: with no usable scheduler interpreter schedule_authority is unavailable and a review takes 3.0 ms median, while an interpreter with fsrs gives fsrs at 83.1 ms median, against 15 ms for a projection read. The 83 ms is the subprocess round trip and the 3 ms case spawns none. Two consequences are now in the contract: a scheduled review is roughly 6x a projection read, and because the wait is inside the writer, reviews and not reads are where requests serialise - so the UI should keep review submissions off its render thread. Pinned by crates/archeaxis-api/tests/contract_review_cost.rs, which launches the binary against an interpreter that cannot exist and against one with fsrs and asserts the authority values differ and the scheduled half is not faster; the fsrs half is skipped where the interpreter lacks the module.
